title: Exceptional Hom transport through fully faithful comparison functors
statement:
Let $\mathcal X_e,\mathcal T_e,\mathcal X_p,\mathcal T_p$ be locally small categories [def-nagata-category]. Let $C_Z:\mathcal X_e\to\mathcal X_p$ and $C_T:\mathcal T_e\to\mathcal T_p$ be fully faithful functors, meaning that their maps on every Hom set are bijective. Suppose given adjunctions $C_T\dashv R$ and $F_e\dashv G_e$, where $F_e:\mathcal X_e\to\mathcal T_e$, and a functor $F_p:\mathcal X_p\to\mathcal T_p$ with a natural isomorphism $b:C_TF_e\xrightarrow{\sim}F_pC_Z$. An adjunction here is a natural Hom-set bijection, with its unit and counit given by the images of identity morphisms. Write $j:\mathrm{id}\to RC_T$ for the first unit, $\mu^e:F_eG_e\to\mathrm{id}$ for the second counit, and $G_p=C_ZG_eR$.
For $H\in\mathcal X_e$, $L\in\mathcal T_p$, define $h_{H,L}$ by the following specified composite, whose middle arrows are those of the given adjunctions:
$$\operatorname{Hom}(F_pC_ZH,L)\xrightarrow{(-)\circ b_H}\operatorname{Hom}(C_TF_eH,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_eH,RL)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(H,G_eRL)\xrightarrow{C_Z}\operatorname{Hom}(C_ZH,G_pL).$$
Then these are natural bijections. For every $N\in\mathcal T_e$, the map $o_N=C_ZG_e(j_N):C_ZG_eN\to G_pC_TN$ is invertible, and
$$h_{G_eN,C_TN}\bigl(C_T(\mu^e_N)\circ b_{G_eN}^{-1}\bigr)=o_N.$$
More precisely, composing $h_{H,C_TN}$ with postcomposition by $o_N^{-1}$ gives exactly the chain consisting of precomposition by $b_H$, the inverse of the fully faithful Hom map of $C_T$, the Hom bijection for $F_e\dashv G_e$, and the Hom map of $C_Z$. Thus the unique preimage of $o_N$ is $C_T(\mu^e_N)\circ b_{G_eN}^{-1}$; after identifying $G_pC_TN$ with $C_ZG_eN$ by $o_N$, this is the counit on these origin objects. This asserts only the displayed Hom bijections, not an adjunction on all objects of $\mathcal X_p$.

proof.text: Write $\alpha_{A,L}:\operatorname{Hom}(C_TA,L)\to\operatorname{Hom}(A,RL)$ and $\beta_{H,N}:\operatorname{Hom}(F_eH,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}(H,G_eN)$ for the two given natural adjunction bijections. The adjunction formulas of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection], applied to these specified bijections, give $\alpha_{A,L}(w)=R(w)\circ j_A$ and $\beta_{G_eN,N}(\mu^e_N)=\mathrm{id}_{G_eN}$. Here the second equality also follows immediately because the counit is the inverse image of the identity. These formulas use the given units and counits, so no choice of a new adjunction is involved.

proof.text: For every $H,L$, precomposition by $b_H$ is a bijection with inverse precomposition by $b_H^{-1}$, the next two arrows $\alpha,\beta$ are bijections by hypothesis, and the last arrow is bijective by full faithfulness of $C_Z$. Their composite is therefore the specified bijection $h_{H,L}$. For $a:H^\prime\to H$ and $s:L\to L^\prime$, naturality of $b$ gives $F_pC_Z(a)\circ b_{H^\prime}=b_H\circ C_TF_e(a)$; naturality of $\alpha$ and $\beta$ and preservation of composition by $C_Z$ then give $h_{H^\prime,L}(q\circ F_pC_Z(a))=h_{H,L}(q)\circ C_Z(a)$ and $h_{H,L^\prime}(s\circ q)=G_p(s)\circ h_{H,L}(q)$. These are precisely naturality in the two variables.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sp-adjunction-unit-fully-faithful-left] to $L=C_T$ and the specified right adjoint $R$. Its only extra hypothesis is full faithfulness of $C_T$, which is assumed, so every $j_N:N\to RC_TN$ is invertible. The morphism $o_N=C_ZG_e(j_N)$ is consequently invertible: its inverse is $C_ZG_e(j_N^{-1})$, since each of $G_e,C_Z$ preserves identities and composition.

source.place: Tag 07RB, lemma-adjoint-fully-faithful (1); functorial preservation of inverse identities.

proof.text: Fix $q:F_pC_ZH\to C_TN$ and put $w=q\circ b_H$. Full faithfulness of $C_T$ supplies the unique $v:F_eH\to N$ with $w=C_T(v)$. The formula in Step 1 and naturality of $j$ give $\alpha_{F_eH,C_TN}(w)=RC_T(v)\circ j_{F_eH}=j_N\circ v$. Naturality of $\beta$ in its second variable therefore gives $\beta_{H,RC_TN}(j_N\circ v)=G_e(j_N)\circ\beta_{H,N}(v)$. Applying $C_Z$ proves $h_{H,C_TN}(q)=o_N\circ C_Z(\beta_{H,N}(v))$. Postcomposition with $o_N^{-1}$ leaves exactly $C_Z(\beta_{H,N}(v))$, where $v$ was obtained by precomposing $q$ with $b_H$ and then applying the inverse fully faithful Hom map of $C_T$. This proves equality with the entire four-arrow chain in the statement, not merely existence of an unspecified bijection.

source.place: Tag 0037, definition-adjoint and following adjunction-map formulas; Tag 0DV0, lemma-compose-counits, explicit composite Hom-bijection argument.

proof.text: Take $H=G_eN$ and $q=C_T(\mu^e_N)\circ b_{G_eN}^{-1}$. Then $q\circ b_{G_eN}=C_T(\mu^e_N)$, so Step 4 has $v=\mu^e_N$ and Step 1 gives $h(q)=o_N\circ C_Z(\mathrm{id}_{G_eN})=o_N$. Since $h$ is injective by Step 2, this $q$ is its unique preimage of $o_N$. Under the identification of its target by $o_N^{-1}$, $o_N$ becomes the identity of $C_ZG_eN$; hence its unique preimage is the counit on the stated origin objects, in the precise identity-preimage sense. Every occurrence of $H$ throughout the argument lies in $\mathcal X_e$, so the argument makes no additional adjunction assertion for arbitrary objects of $\mathcal X_p$.

lean.statement: theorem fullyFaithful_transport (CZ : Xe ⥤ Xp) (CT : Te ⥤ Tp) [CZ.Full] [CZ.Faithful] [CT.Full] [CT.Faithful] (Fe : Xe ⥤ Te) (Ge : Te ⥤ Xe) (R : Tp ⥤ Te) (Fp : Xp ⥤ Tp) (adjT : CT ⊣ R) (adjE : Fe ⊣ Ge) (b : Fe ⋙ CT ≅ CZ ⋙ Fp) : (∀ (H : Xe) (L : Tp), Function.Bijective (homMap CZ adjT adjE b H L)) ∧ (∀ (H' H : Xe) (L : Tp) (a : H' ⟶ H) (q : Fp.obj (CZ.obj H) ⟶ L), homMap CZ adjT adjE b H' L (Fp.map (CZ.map a) ≫ q) = CZ.map a ≫ homMap CZ adjT adjE b H L q) ∧ (∀ (H : Xe) (L L' : Tp) (q : Fp.obj (CZ.obj H) ⟶ L) (s : L ⟶ L'), homMap CZ adjT adjE b H L' (q ≫ s) = homMap CZ adjT adjE b H L q ≫ (R ⋙ Ge ⋙ CZ).map s) ∧ (∀ N : Te, IsIso (originMap CZ Ge adjT N) ∧ homMap CZ adjT adjE b (Ge.obj N) (CT.obj N) (b.inv.app (Ge.obj N) ≫ CT.map (adjE.counit.app N)) = originMap CZ Ge adjT N ∧ (∀ (H : Xe) (q : Fp.obj (CZ.obj H) ⟶ CT.obj N), homMap CZ adjT adjE b H (CT.obj N) q ≫ inv (originMap CZ Ge adjT N) = CZ.map (adjE.homEquiv H N (CT.preimage (b.hom.app H ≫ q)))) ∧ (∀ q : Fp.obj (CZ.obj (Ge.obj N)) ⟶ CT.obj N, homMap CZ adjT adjE b (Ge.obj N) (CT.obj N) q = originMap CZ Ge adjT N ↔ q = b.inv.app (Ge.obj N) ≫ CT.map (adjE.counit.app N)) ∧ (∀ q : Fp.obj (CZ.obj (Ge.obj N)) ⟶ CT.obj N, homMap CZ adjT adjE b (Ge.obj N) (CT.obj N) q ≫ inv (originMap CZ Ge adjT N) = 𝟙 (CZ.obj (Ge.obj N)) ↔ q = b.inv.app (Ge.obj N) ≫ CT.map (adjE.counit.app N)))
